g.text: Attribution graphs over parameter components — VPD §5

text.style: font-size: 13.49px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Node size is the direct effect on log p(target) when that component's owned mass is scaled by 4. An arc c′→c is DE(c) − DE(c | c′ already perturbed):

text.style: font-size: 13.49px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: how much of c's effect depends on c′ having run first. Order is by depth, the mass-weighted mean layer of a component's parameters. VPD ABLATES here; that

text.style: font-size: 13.49px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: fails on this decomposition — a geometric partition of trained weights, not something optimised for ablation sufficiency. Zeroing a whole component moves

text.style: font-size: 13.49px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: log p by ~0.002 nats; scaling it by 4 moves it by up to 5.
